The Good Deposit
de-POS-it
noun phrase
From the Greek parathēkē, “a thing committed in trust, a deposit” (from paratithēmi, “to set before, to entrust”), naming the sound doctrine committed to the believer to be guarded.

Biblical Definition

The good deposit is the treasure of sound doctrine and the gospel committed in trust to the believer, which he is charged to keep safe by the power of the Holy Ghost. Paul charges Timothy, his son in the faith: That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us (2Ti 1:14). The word he uses is the merchant’s word for a deposit, a thing laid up in another’s hands to be kept whole and rendered up untouched. Just before, the apostle had set his own example: I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day (2Ti 1:12). So there are two deposits answering each other. The believer commits his soul to Christ, who is able to keep it; and Christ commits to the believer the good thing of sound doctrine, which he is to guard. The dictionary marks this as the charge of every faithful minister and church: the form of sound words (2Ti 1:13), the faith once delivered unto the saints (Jude 1:3), is not the church’s to amend, lessen, or improve, but a sacred trust to be held fast and handed on unaltered. So the Scripture teaches the closed and finished deposit of revealed truth, guarded against every novelty and corruption; and the guarding is not by human cleverness but by the Holy Ghost who dwelleth in us.

Webster 1828 Definition

The sound doctrine and gospel committed in trust to the believer, to be kept whole by the Holy Ghost.

THE GOOD DEPOSIT, the sound doctrine committed in trust to the believer to be guarded.

The word means a thing laid up in another’s hands to be kept whole.

Timothy is charged to keep it by the Holy Ghost that dwelleth in us.

The believer commits his soul to Christ, who is able to keep it.

The faith once delivered is a trust to be held fast and handed on unaltered.

Key Scripture

2Ti 1:14 — "That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us."

2Ti 1:12 — "For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day."

2Ti 1:13 — "Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus."

Jud 1:3 — "Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints."

Modern Corruption

A treasure of Scripture; the sound doctrine entrusted to the church to be guarded whole and handed on unaltered.

expand to see more

The good deposit has drawn little redefinition from the present age as a phrase, though the trust it names is ever under assault. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the charge to keep the sound doctrine committed to the church, neither amending nor lessening it.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the faith once delivered to the saints is a fixed and finished deposit, the church’s to guard and hand on, not to amend or improve. The form of sound words is a sacred trust, laid up in the believer’s hands to be kept whole and rendered up untouched against that day. This guarding is not by human cleverness but by the Holy Ghost who dwelleth in us. Let the reader hold fast the deposit against every novelty and corruption, and earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.

Hebrew Roots

From the Greek parathēkē, “a deposit committed in trust,” the phrase names the sound doctrine the believer must guard.

The Good Deposit — Greek parathēkē, “a thing committed in trust.”

It is the treasure of sound doctrine entrusted to the believer and the church.

Timothy is charged to keep it by the Holy Ghost that dwelleth in us.

The faith once delivered is not the church’s to amend or lessen.

It is a closed and finished trust, guarded against every corruption.
